title: Blue skies and red sunsets
description: Discover why the sky is blue and sunsets turn red. Two short science lessons connect everyday sky colours to the journey of sunlight.
introduction:
A blue afternoon becomes an orange evening. What changed?

Start with the colours hidden in sunlight, then follow its longer path through the evening air. These two short lessons fit together; read at your own pace and try the optional quizzes.
prerequisites: No science background needed. Each new term is explained as it appears.

lessons.objective: Connect the blue daytime sky to sunlight scattered by air molecules.
Explain how the low Sun’s longer air path changes the colours reaching us.

glossary.definition: The layer of gases around Earth.
Light being redirected in different directions.
The distance from one wave peak to the next.
Scattering by very small particles such as air molecules, which redirects shorter wavelengths more strongly.

outcomes: Explain why a blue sky does not need a nearby sea.
Compare the wavelengths of blue and red light.
Connect a low Sun with a longer route through the air and warmer arriving light.
